basis: First actual original-pixel opens in this fresh context. Written before any candidate PNG or candidate spec was inspected. No author inventory was read or used.
candidateMappingLocation: report.json figures[].sourceMapping; this source-first inventory is not rewritten from the candidate object list.

items.fact: One round optical apparatus disk with a heavy circular perimeter, horizontal interior ruled/hatch strokes and inward-pointing triangular rim markers.
relationships: The semicylinder is inside this shared disk frame.
The light source is outside the disk on its lower-left side.
A vertical support extends below the disk.
items.detailHOLD: The printing does not warrant an exact count or angular calibration of the rim markers or ruled strokes. They are apparatus detail, not a coordinate grid with readable numeric ticks.

items.fact: A lower semicircular element has a roughly horizontal flat top near the disk center and a curved lower edge; its texture differs from the surrounding disk.
relationships: Flat face lies across the central region of the disk.
Curved body lies below that face.
Two dark, approximately circular mounting details appear near the ends of the flat face.
items.detailHOLD: Exact mounting geometry and hatch-obscured optical traces are not recoverable as measurements from this extraction.

items.fact: A lamp-like object outside the lower-left perimeter points diagonally toward the central semicylinder region. One dark stand descends from the disk bottom.
relationships: Illuminator belongs to the lower half of the apparatus, not the air region above the flat face.
The lamp is directed inward toward the semicylinder.
items.detailHOLD: No readable lamp model, calibrated angular position or numerical value is present.

items.fact: The small printed/hatch-heavy semicylinder region does not allow me to assign every incident, reflected and refracted beam trace or its direction independently with confidence.
No confidently readable angle symbol, medium name, numerical angle, normal label or case letter appears in these source pixels.

editionContextRequirementsNotClaimedAsPi: Glass is the higher-index first medium and air is the second; n > 1 is relative to air.
Incident light arrives from inside the lower glass semicylinder, and reflected light remains inside it.
The reflected angle equals the incidence angle, both measured from the interface normal.
For nonzero subcritical incidence with propagating refraction, refraction bends away from the normal and beta > alpha.
Clear ray arrows, a normal, English medium labels and angle marks may clarify the approved prose, but must not be reported as recovered source-pixel details.

items.fact: One shared horizontal interface crosses a vertical normal at a common vertex. A lower semicircular outline spans the interface endpoints and surrounds the lower ray branches.
relationships: Normal is perpendicular to the interface.
All ray and angle marks share the interface/normal intersection.
Semicircular apparatus body is below the flat interface.

items.fact: A slanted branch runs from lower left to the common vertex, crossing the semicircular outline.
relationships: Incident branch is on the lower-left side of the normal.
Its angle to the lower normal is marked alpha_0.
items.detailHOLD: An incident-direction arrowhead is not independently clear in the source; inward direction is supplied by the approved experiment prose, not manufactured as a pixel observation.

items.fact: A slanted lower-right branch leaves the vertex and has a visible outward arrowhead at its far end.
relationships: Reflected branch lies below the interface, opposite the incident branch across the normal.
Its lower-right angle to the normal is marked gamma.
The two lower branch angles appear paired about the common normal.

items.fact: A dashed horizontal branch extends from the common vertex to the right along the interface and terminates in a rightward arrow.
relationships: Grazing direction is along the interface, not a slanted propagating ray into the upper medium.
An upper-right quarter-angle arc between the upward normal and horizontal rightward direction is labelled beta = 90.
items.detailHOLD: The extraction visibly reads beta = 90; the degree glyph is not separately clear enough to certify its exact source typography.

items.fact: Readable symbolic labels are alpha_0, gamma and beta = 90. There is no printed medium name, refractive-index value, case letter or separate strict-greater-than-critical panel.
relationships: alpha_0 belongs to the incident-to-normal angle.
gamma belongs to the reflected-to-normal angle.
beta = 90 belongs to the grazing direction measured from the upper normal.

editionContextRequirementsNotClaimedAsPi: For this apparatus, the lower first medium is glass and the upper second medium is air, with n > 1.
At alpha = alpha_0, beta = 90 degrees is the grazing limiting direction; reflected light remains in glass.
Strictly greater incidence alpha > alpha_0 has no refracted beam propagating into air, and is total internal reflection in the approved ideal transparent, nonabsorbing-interface model.
A separate strict-greater-angle case is a modern prose-derived addition, not a second source subfigure.
Do not add measured beam-energy percentages or infer detailed source-ray calibration from the source drawing.
